items.rule: Tangents at endpoints of a diameter are parallel.
items.example: Diameter AB acts as the transversal.

items.rule: A parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
items.example: Use equal tangent segments from each vertex.

items.rule: Opposite sides of a tangential quadrilateral subtend supplementary angles at the center.

items.rule: The angle between two tangents is supplementary to the central angle between the contact radii.
items.example: Use the two right angles at the tangent points.

concepts.title: 1. Parallel Tangents at Diameter Endpoints
concepts.subtitle: Parallelism via perpendicularity
concepts.summary: Tangents at the endpoints of a diameter are parallel because the diameter makes 90° with both tangents, giving equal alternate interior angles.

points.text: Equal alternate interior angles imply $PQ\parallel RS$.
